scenes.headline: Why a language model's output layer has a rank ceiling
scenes.sub: The softmax bottleneck, and the mixture that breaks through it.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Melon! Every language model ends in a softmax. Here's the wall hidden inside it, and the mixture that gets through.

scenes.text: Logits are a product of two skinny matrices, so what they can express has rank at most the hidden size d, however good the network is.
scenes.mark: rank at most the hidden size d
scenes.say: The idea: logits are a product of two skinny matrices, so their rank is at most the hidden size, however good the network is.

parts.note: every context's hidden state, one row each, d wide
parts.say: H holds every context's hidden state, one row each, d numbers wide.

parts.note: every word's embedding, also d wide
parts.say: W holds every word's embedding, also d wide.

parts.note: row shifts under softmax buy one rank, no more
parts.say: So their product has rank at most d. Softmax ignores row shifts, but that freedom is worth exactly one rank.

steps.say: The fix: one linear layer turns the hidden state into K context vectors instead of one.
Each goes through the same embedding table and its own softmax. K readings of one table, not K tables.
Context weights then average the probabilities. The log of that sum is nonlinear, so there's no rank ceiling.

steps.note: mix the hidden states instead, and it is one softmax again
steps.say: The order is the whole trick. Average the context vectors before a single softmax instead, and the rank stays capped at d.

scenes.title: Measured rank, Penn Treebank
scenes.say: Measured on Penn Treebank: softmax hits rank four hundred, the bound to the digit. Mixed contexts, two eighty. Mixture of softmaxes, nine thousand nine hundred eighty-one.

scenes.label: bits per character on text8, softmax and MoS: no bottleneck to break
scenes.note: character-level rank is at most about 27
scenes.say: And the control: at character level the bound can't bind, and mixture of softmaxes changes nothing. Both score one point four nine bits per character.

scenes.text: The network isn't the limit; the interface is. Mixing probabilities after the softmax, not features before it, lifts the ceiling.
scenes.say: So the network isn't the limit. The interface is. Mix after the softmax, not before it, and the ceiling lifts.

recap: Logits are H times W: rank at most d
Mix probabilities after softmax, not hidden states
It costs 2-3x, so it never shipped
scenes.say: To recap: a rank-d wall, a mixture around it, and a cost that kept it out of your model.
